After I filter my DCG emulsion, I occasionally have a couple of small bubbles. I usually take a q-tip and pull the bubble out with it. But I was reading this site and they mention a fine spray of alcohol.

"Remove the bubbles by spraying a small amount of alcohol onto them. The alcohol reduces the surface tension so the bubbles can break. Use the normal atomizer used to spray water when using the stencil technique of enameling."

[http://www.enamellers.nl/english/carpenter6.htm](http://www.enamellers.nl/english/carpenter6.htm)

Seems they say Type B (bone) is better for emulsion then Type A.

posts.author: meekan01
posts.content_md: A trick we used to use to get bubbles out of PDMS for high resolution contact lithography was to put it under vacuum after casting. The reduced vapor pressure in the atmosphere pulls out the bubbles very, very well. A bell jar works brilliantly, but you don't really even need that high of a vacuum- just keep in mind that if you lower the pressure too quickly, the gelatin may boil and make a big mess. Do it gradually =)

Michael, very true but...

> Gelatin recovered from bone is used primarily in photographic applications

[http://www.gelatin-gmia.com/html/rawmaterials.html](http://www.gelatin-gmia.com/html/rawmaterials.html)

Definition of better (hahaha);

[http://dict.die.net/better/](http://dict.die.net/better/)

Dave, yes I can usually get the few bubbles out of the beaker easily but thought the alcohol thingy was interesting and I should try it. If I see a bubble sliding down the glass during coating I hesitate continue to pour in that area until it is washed off the plate. I hold the plate by hand and I recapture the emulsion in a container that I hold the plate over during coating. This container is heated thus I can pour it back into the beaker and continue coating. Whenever pouring or coating to keep bubles from forming I found it is like pouring headless beer. Tilt and pour closely to surface.

I use double Mr. Coffee Filters to filter in a ceramic funnel shaped filter holder by gravity. I bought one of these and use the ceramic filter part but not the vacuum. I tried the vacuum and it bubbles the gel terribly. It came with the hand vacuum pump, hose, stopper, ceramic filter holder, beaker and some 5 micron filters. I only tried the filters once and the gel would not flow trough them too easily. I took a long time and the gel was hardening.
